title: The Midnight Oath Revisited
premise: August Montrose has spent her life in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, hiding as the last swordspeaker after a purge erased her order and her country. When she finds tonight's date inscribed in a century-old prophecy book, she learns the thirteenth moon will seal the borders of Vessany—a nation that officially no longer exists—trapping every oath-bound soul inside forever. Guided by a disgraced cartographer of impossible roads and haunted by the memory-ghost of her dead mentor, August must recover the scattered words of her original oath to open the Door Out. In the end, she speaks the oath anew with her own name in it, dissolving the old magic's claim on her blood and choosing an ordinary life over power—but only after sacrificing the mentor's ghost, who was the prophecy's author all along.
about_author: W. M. Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps of countries that no longer appear on any atlas. They write fantasy about people who survive by being forgotten.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses
chapters.summary: August's POV. She tends her quiet life in the Hollow, sharpening a sword that never needs sharpening, until a traveling peddler trades her a water-stained book of prophecies. Tonight's date glows faintly on its page. The emotional beat: dread cracking through routine, the first hint that invisibility was always borrowed, not owned.

chapters.title: Ink Older Than Grief
chapters.summary: August's POV. She deciphers the prophecy: on the thirteenth turn of the moon, Vessany's borders will close for good, sealing all oath-bound blood inside. A marginal sketch shows a door standing in a field of ash. Emotional beat: vertigo—the past reaching forward to claim her, and the humiliating realization she knows almost nothing about her own order.

chapters.title: What the Hollow Keeps Out
chapters.summary: August's POV. She tests the valley's edge and confirms magic still cannot cross it—but something on the other side now waits there, patient as weather. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; home revealed as cage. She decides she must leave before the moon completes its cycle, betraying the one rule her mentor died teaching her.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Roads That Aren't
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Introduce Sable Vane, exiled mapmaker who draws routes into places that were erased from existence. She agrees to guide August toward the Door Out—for a price: August's true name, spoken aloud. Emotional beat: wary transactional trust between two women who have both survived by being unrecorded.

chapters.title: Crossing the Threshold of Ash
chapters.summary: August's POV. They leave the Hollow at night; crossing the boundary feels like drowning in reverse. Magic floods back into August's bones, and her sword begins whispering fragments of her oath. Emotional beat: terror and intoxication braided together—power returning like a fever she'd forgotten she survived.

chapters.title: The Country With No Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. They walk through Vessany's remains: villages that remember being conquered, innkeepers who flinch at the word 'oath.' August learns the purge wasn't just slaughter—it was editing; records rewritten so swordspeakers never existed. Emotional beat: grief for a homeland that was murdered twice, once in flesh and once in paper.

chapters.title: A Ghost Made of Lessons
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her dead mentor, Ilse, manifests from the sword's whispers—young-seeming, sharp-tongued, claiming the oath's words are hidden at three sites. August doesn't question why a ghost would know. Emotional beat: bittersweet reunion shadowed by the reader's first subtle hint that Ilse avoids certain questions too smoothly.

chapters.title: The First Word: Belltower of the Unringed
chapters.summary: August's POV. At a belltower whose bells were melted, August recovers the oath's first word by ringing silence itself. The act marks her—her shadow now moves a half-second late. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into unease; each word recovered makes her more visible to whatever hunts oath-bound blood.

chapters.title: The Moon Counts Aloud
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Fourth moon-turn. Pursuers appear: the Custodians, clerks-turned-inquisitors who enforce the erasure of Vessany. Sable reveals she once mapped for them, which is why she was exiled. Emotional beat: betrayal narrowly averted by honesty; the two women choose each other despite their ledgers of sins.

chapters.title: The Second Word: River That Remembers
chapters.summary: August's POV. In a river that flows backward through memory, August relives her childhood—the purge, Ilse's death, her flight to the Hollow—and pulls the second word from the water. Emotional beat: forced confrontation with trauma; she stops running from the memory and instead reads it closely, noticing details that don't fit.

chapters.title: Details That Don't Fit
chapters.summary: August's POV. The memory shows Ilse dying before the final word was ever spoken—so how does the ghost know it? August confronts Ilse, who deflects with a lesson about trust. Emotional beat: suspicion planted and suppressed; love arguing with evidence, and evidence quietly winning ground.

chapters.title: The Custodians' Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Captured briefly by Custodians, Sable reads their master ledger: every erased name, including 'August Montrose' already written in the column marked SEALED. She escapes but understands the prophecy isn't prediction—it's paperwork being executed. Emotional beat: cold horror; bureaucracy as villainy, fate as filing system.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Approaching
chapters.summary: August's POV. Twelfth moon. The land itself begins forgetting them—roads lengthen, Sable's maps blank themselves, August's reflection lags further behind. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into desperation; the world is closing like a book being shut around them.

chapters.title: The Third Word: Field of Ash
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the ash-field from the prophecy's margin, they find the Door Out—locked, needing the full oath. Ilse offers the third word freely, too readily. August speaks it, and the Door opens onto darkness. Emotional beat: relief undercut by dread; the trap is nearly sprung and only August senses it.

chapters.title: The Author of the Prophecy
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV (the book's single chapter inside the antagonist's head). Reveal: Ilse wrote the prophecy a century ago, bound herself into the sword, and engineered everything so August would speak the complete oath—not to free her, but to transfer the oath's binding into Ilse's restored body. Emotional beat: chilling tenderness; the mentor's love was real and also a leash.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Dead Country
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the threshold, Ilse demands August step through first—into the dark that is actually the oath's mouth. August finally says the truth aloud: the dates, the ghost, the convenient words. Ilse drops the mask. Emotional beat: heartbreak as climax approaches; betrayal by the person who taught her what love looked like.

chapters.title: Swordspeak
chapters.summary: August's POV. Climax. Ilse seizes the half-spoken oath; the Door becomes a furnace of stolen names. August refuses to finish the recitation—instead she breaks the oath's grammar, speaking it wrong on purpose, inserting her own name where the ritual demands Ilse's. Emotional beat: defiant self-authorship; identity wielded as the one weapon power cannot corrupt.

chapters.title: What Breaks When an Oath Breaks
chapters.summary: August's POV. The mis-spoken oath unravels both bindings: Ilse scatters into honest, wordless light, and the Door collapses, taking Vessany's sealing magic with it. August loses the swordspeaker's power entirely—her sword goes silent forever. Emotional beat: devastating release; victory that costs her the magic, the ghost, and the country all at once.

chapters.title: Borders, Unwritten
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Dawn. The Custodians' ledger burns blank; erased names resurface in living memories across the valley. Sable begins drawing a new map—one that includes Vessany under a new name chosen by its survivors. Emotional beat: cautious hope; the work of remembering beginning where the work of escaping ended.

chapters.title: The Ordinary Life
chapters.summary: August's POV. August returns to the Hollow, which no longer needs to hide anyone. She hangs up the silent sword, plants a garden where the peddler's stall stood, and starts writing down everything she remembers—in her own hand, with her own name signed. Emotional beat: quiet reclamation; memory as choice rather than burden.

chapters.title: Visitors Who Remember
chapters.summary: August's POV. Survivors of the erasure begin arriving in the valley, drawn by rumor of the woman who broke a hundred-year oath. Among them, a child asks August to teach her 'the loud way of talking to steel.' Emotional beat: warmth and responsibility; legacy offered rather than imposed.

chapters.title: The Oath, Revisited
chapters.summary: August's POV. Final scene: on the thirteenth moon's last night, August stands at the valley's edge, neither leaving nor sealed, and speaks a new vow of her own devising—to witness, to record, to stay reachable. Far off, a bell that was never melted rings once. Emotional beat: serene closure; the girl who stayed invisible chooses, freely, to be seen.
